studies.label: Writer experiment (short-story writing with optional GPT-4 story ideas), rated by a separate evaluator sample
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No clustered treatment assignment. Evaluator-rated outcomes use robust standard errors clustered by evaluator, not by randomized writer. Writer-story similarity outcomes use robust standard errors, with one story per writer (PDF p. 8, Statistical analysis).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 7, Materials and Methods, Writer study and experimental conditions; AI-arm counts in PDF p. 2, Results, Baseline versus generative AI conditions
counts_source.quote: therefore dropped from the analysis, result- ing in a total number of writers and stories of 293.

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Write without any mention of or access to generative AI. Writers admitting outside AI use were excluded. The analyzed arm count is not printed (PDF pp. 2, 7).

arms.name: Human with one GenAI idea
arms.description: Optional request for one three-sentence GPT-4 story idea from a fixed prompt; the writer then writes the story and cannot copy and paste the idea. Analyzed count is printed in PDF p. 2, Results: Of the 100 writers in the Human with one GenAI idea condition.

arms.name: Human with five GenAI ideas
arms.description: Optional requests for up to five three-sentence GPT-4 story ideas from fixed prompts; all requested ideas remain visible and cannot be copied and pasted. Analyzed count is printed in PDF p. 2, Results: 93 of 98 writers in this condition requested an idea.

studies.task: Write an English story of exactly eight sentences, suitable for a teenage and young adult audience, about a randomly assigned adventure on the open seas, in the jungle, or on a different planet (PDF p. 7).

ai_tool.name: OpenAI GPT-4 via OpenAI's GPT API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Writer study and experimental conditions, paragraph describing randomized conditions and the fixed story-idea prompt; model release year not printed

preregistration.where: AsPredicted.org, ID 136723; PDF p. 8, Preregistration and ethics approval. A copy is cited as Supplementary section S9, which is not in the supplied PDF.
preregistration.primary_outcome: Evaluator-rated novelty and usefulness indices (PDF p. 8, Outcome variables; PDF p. 2, Baseline versus generative AI conditions).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Lay Prolific evaluators rated the stories before disclosure of AI access or use. Nine-point agreement scale from one (not at all) to nine (extremely); PDF p. 8, Outcome variables. Mean of the novel, original, and rare items.

regression.model: OLS with indicators for both AI conditions and Human-only as reference. Rating-level analysis; robust standard errors clustered by evaluator. Here clustered_participant refers to evaluator participants, not the writers randomized to assistance (PDF p. 8, Statistical analysis).

paper_effect.standardizer: Percentage increase relative to the Human-only condition mean, as printed; units are percent, not standardized deviations.

estimates.notes: The reported analysis uses ratings as observations and robust standard errors clustered by evaluator, not by the writer assigned to AI. se_basis is coded rating because the schema has no evaluator category; this does not mean that the paper treats all ratings as independent. The reported uncertainty does not account for repeated ratings of the same randomized writer and should not enter pooling as writer-level uncertainty. n_units is the reported size of the full evaluator analysis across all randomized conditions, not the number of ratings in just the two named arms. The Human-only writer count and two-arm writer totals are not printed and are not calculated. No numerical standard error, confidence-interval endpoints, outcome SD, or standardized mean difference is printed in the supplied main article. Figure intervals were inspected but not digitized.

open_items: The separate Supplementary Materials (sections S1-S9, tables S1-S18, figures S1-S6, listed on PDF p. 8) are not included in the supplied PDF and no local supplement was found. Numerical combined-AI contrasts, component coefficients, remaining emotional-characteristic contrasts, and robustness-model results cannot be confirmed from this file.

The main PDF does not print the Human-only analyzed count, the number randomized overall or by arm, or two-arm analyzed totals. These are left null rather than calculated from the other counts or copied from a data-audit record.

Arm means are mostly absent, and no outcome SDs or numerical standard errors or interval bounds are printed. The only printed arm means are one-idea usefulness and Human-only similarity to an AI idea. No unavailable means or uncertainty statistics were derived.
Rating-outcome uncertainty is clustered by evaluator, not by randomized writer. Writer-level analysis or valid uncertainty accounting for writer dependence is needed before pooling those effects.
Neither arm level for the across-writer similarity measure is printed. The article reports raw coefficients, p-values, and percentages of the control range; the figures were not digitized.
The paper does not state whether the two similarity outcomes were preregistered or primary, and it does not identify the embedding model or GPT-4 release year.
The random AI-idea comparison pool is described as within story topic on PDF p. 5 and within condition on PDF p. 8. This discrepancy affects the anchoring measure.
The main text does not specify the test used for the five-ideas-versus-one-idea usefulness comparison; only its p-value, percentage increase, and comparator mean are printed.
The supplied main article does not print per-arm numbers of evaluations. n_units records the full reported analysis count; it is not a count restricted to the two named arms.
notes: Extraction checked 2026-10-09 against the supplied PDF with PyMuPDF. The entire markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks, including references and the publisher information page. All four figures were inspected; no tables were detected in the main PDF and the listed supplementary sections are absent. One randomized writer experiment is represented: evaluators rate its outputs and do not form another experiment of AI-assisted production. AI access was optional; the paper’s intention-to-treat terminology retains writers who declined an AI idea, but participants were also excluded for noncompletion and admitted outside AI use (PDF pp. 6-7). All reported eligible full-sample contrasts are retained, including figure-only and combined-AI contrasts with null numeric statistics. The AI-anchoring outcome omitted under the screening form’s outcome cap is included with form_outcome_id null. Numeric results are transcribed, not calculated. Percentage changes are retained under paper_effect type other in their printed percent units; they are not standardized effects. Raw regression coefficients remain in regression.coef, with their signs unchanged. Printed precision, including trailing zeros and the minus sign, is preserved in the source quotations. Sources reproduce PDF-extracted text with whitespace collapsed; discretionary and line-break hyphens are retained. Metadata and scale descriptions are supported by the cited methods pages. No supplementary dataset values, inferred control counts, or recomputed statistics were used. No other screened paper is identified in the reconciled form as sharing these participants.
